clue.text: A comment added in adapted clue for small container

indicators.note: a thing added in is slipped inside something else, so one piece goes into the middle of another
something adapted has been altered to suit a new use, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written
PS, a postscript, is a comment added at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A setter tinkers with a clue, slipping in an extra remark, all to describe a tiny box.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'clue' sound like the setter's own work, but it is just four letters to rearrange; 'A comment' is read as two pieces, the article and the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A capsule is a small sealed case or pod, such as a time capsule, a seed capsule or a pill casing.

clue.text: Body container largely carried in vehicles

indicators.note: largely means mostly but not wholly, so the final letter is dropped
what is carried in something sits inside it, so one piece is held within another

parts.note: cars are vehicles
a case is a container, here without its last letter

explanation.surface: A body bag or coffin is mostly transported in vehicles, as at a funeral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Container' wants to be part of the definition alongside 'Body', but it is the wordplay: a case, cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: A carcass is a dead body, especially of an animal, though also used jokingly of a person's own frame.

clue.text: Not up — up? A hoax

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters are written from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzled exchange: something is not up, then someone asks whether it is up, and suspects a trick.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'up' reads like nonsense; the first 'Not up' is the fodder, the second 'up?' tells you to write it upwards in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A put-on is a deception or prank played on someone, the noun from 'to put someone on'.

clue.text: In a tumult you all end not intermingled

indicators.note: a tumult is a noisy disorderly commotion, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Amid chaos, everyone finishes up staying apart from each other.
explanation.walkthrough: The nine letters of 'you all end' rearrange exactly into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Unalloyed literally describes metal not mixed with another, so pure and free of any blending.

clue.text: Chosen some travel items

indicators.note: some means only a portion, so the letters are a run taken from within the following words

parts.note: the run spans the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Someone has picked out a few things to take on a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across 'travEL ITEms'.
explanation.definitionFit: The elite are the select few, those picked out as the best of a group.

clue.text: Officer's attendant welcomes ordinary sailor

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a batman is an army officer's personal servant
O is a standard abbreviation for ordinary

explanation.surface: An officer's orderly greets a humble naval rating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordinary sailor' looks like one phrase meaning able seaman, but 'ordinary' is the O going inside BATMAN, a British army term for an officer's servant.
explanation.definitionFit: A boatman works on boats for a living, rowing or ferrying, so a kind of seafarer or waterman.

clue.text: Large American remains with first and last of traitorous union fraudsters

parts.note: big means large
AM is a short form of American
to remain is to be, to exist, so 'remains' can be 'is'

indicators.note: the first and last letters are the two ends of a word, so only those are kept

parts.note: the two end letters of this word

explanation.surface: A big American's corpse is found alongside members of a treacherous trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remains' suggests a dead body, but it is the verb, giving IS; 'union' is not a trade union but marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Bigamists cheat by entering a second marriage while still legally wed, so they are fraudsters in matrimony.

clue.text: Gather together great number in a religious service

parts.note: taken as written
Mass is the Catholic eucharistic service

explanation.surface: A large crowd assembles at a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: MASS does double duty: it is the service, and 'a great number' is a mass of people, so the phrase hints at the same word twice.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to collect or accumulate a large quantity, bringing things into one heap.

clue.text: Tiniest bit sick, one in September, for example

indicators.note: to be in something is to sit inside it, so these pieces go within another

parts.note: September is an example of a month
ill means sick
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone feels faintly unwell, perhaps an individual in autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'September, for example' is a definition by example, so the solver must go up to the category it belongs to.
explanation.definitionFit: A millionth is one part in a million, a minute fraction, so the smallest of portions.

clue.text: Smell brightly coloured bunch of flowers

parts.note: to nose is to smell or sniff out
an older sense of gay is bright and showy

explanation.surface: Sniffing a vivid posy.
explanation.walkthrough: GAY is used in its older meaning of bright or cheerful, as in gay colours.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosegay is a small posy of sweet-smelling blooms, originally carried to mask bad odours.

clue.text: Going back over with reference to copy

parts.note: re means concerning or with reference to
a tracing is a copy made through thin paper

explanation.surface: Reviewing a document again with reference to a duplicate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copy' looks like a verb but is the noun TRACING, a drawing copied through transparent paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Retracing steps means following the same route again, so revisiting a path already taken.

clue.text: Collection of maps finally lacking last of text

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so a letter is removed

parts.note: at last means finally

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, so only that one is taken

parts.note: the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: A book of maps ends up without its last page of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' looks like it selects a final letter, but it is the phrase AT LAST, which then drops its own last T.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlas is a bound volume of charts and geographic plates.

clue.text: Cancel yearbook, second of two articles absent

indicators.note: absent means missing, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: an annual is a book published once a year
the word has two letters that are the article 'a'; the second of them goes

explanation.surface: A school decides to scrap its yearbook, with a couple of pieces missing.
explanation.walkthrough: ANNUAL contains two As, each being the indefinite article; removing the second leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul is to declare void or invalid, as a marriage or contract, which is to revoke it.

clue.text: Entanglement — curiously, Englishmen left out

definitions.note: noun; the answer is the gerund, used as a noun

indicators.note: curiously means in an odd way, so the letters are arranged strangely
out means removed or excluded, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A tangled situation where, oddly, the English were excluded.
explanation.walkthrough: Take L out of ENGLISHMEN and rearrange the remaining nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Enmeshing is the act of catching something in a net, so a being caught up or tangled.

clue.text: Puss angry about ways of scattering paint

indicators.note: about can mean around or roundabout, so the letters are turned round into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cross cat knocks over the decorator's tins and splatters paint everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Angry' looks like an anagram signal but is part of the fodder; 'about' does the stirring.
explanation.definitionFit: Spray guns atomise and blow paint onto a surface, so they are tools for spreading a fine coat.

clue.text: Gleam of light involving advisor now and then with record for branch of medicine

indicators.note: to involve something is to include it, so one piece wraps round the others

parts.note: a ray is a beam or gleam of light

indicators.note: now and then means occasionally, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters
a log is a written record

explanation.surface: A faint glow surrounds a consultant who keeps notes on some medical specialty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Now and then' keeps the even-placed letters here, not the odd ones; only that choice fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Radiology is the medical specialty using X-rays and scans to diagnose and treat illness.

clue.text: In an uncommon way, peacekeepers and US columns essentially unite

parts.note: the United Nations sends peacekeeping forces
taken as written

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence or core, so only the central letter is kept

parts.note: the central letter of a seven-letter word
to ally is to unite or join forces

explanation.surface: Peacekeeping forces and American troops, rarely, join up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Columns' suggests marching troops; only its central letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Unusually is an adverb meaning out of the ordinary, rarely seen or exceptionally.

clue.text: One hears little lad is bright

indicators.note: what one hears is the sound, not the spelling, so a word sounding the same is wanted

parts.note: sonny is a familiar way to address a young boy

explanation.surface: Word gets around that a small boy is clever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bright' looks like it means clever, but it is the weather sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunny describes a day full of sunshine, and also a cheerful disposition, both well lit.

clue.text: Deem, it's said, person of merit able to endure in the main

definitions.text: able to endure in the main

indicators.note: what is said is spoken, so the sound of the word counts rather than its spelling

parts.note: to see something as so is to deem it so
a worthy is a distinguished, deserving person

explanation.surface: A verdict on a deserving person: they are judged capable of holding out for the most part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' looks like 'mostly', but the main is an old word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaworthy vessel is fit to withstand voyages on the ocean without coming to grief.

clue.text: Redecorated, somewhat splendider on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection shows things mirror-wise, so the letters run backwards
somewhat means to some extent, so only part of a word is used

parts.note: the last five letters

explanation.surface: Thinking it over, the redecorated room is rather more splendid.
explanation.walkthrough: The tail of 'splenDIDER' read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To redo a room is to decorate it afresh, so the past tense means did up again.

clue.text: Earfuls about horse's unwillingness to jump

indicators.note: about can mean round about, so the letters are turned round into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rider gives a stubborn horse a stern telling-off for balking at a fence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' reads as 'on the subject of', but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: In show jumping a refusal is when the horse stops short of an obstacle instead of clearing it.

clue.text: Somehow staunched and not injured

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified manner, so the letters can come in any order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Bleeding was stopped somehow, and the patient was not really hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: The nine letters of 'staunched' rearrange to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Unscathed means coming through danger without harm, wound or damage of any kind.

clue.text: Carrying submachine-gun, did exaggerate

indicators.note: to carry is to hold, so one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: taken as written
the Sten was a British submachine-gun of the Second World War

explanation.surface: An armed man overstated how he had acted.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sten is the submachine-gun crosswords reach for most often; 'did' looks like part of the sentence but is fodder taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: To distend is to swell or stretch out, so figuratively to enlarge or inflate beyond normal.

clue.text: Pay for animal enclosure work unit

parts.note: to foot the bill is to pay for it
a pound is a pen for stray animals

explanation.surface: Someone funds a pen for livestock as a work project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pay' suggests money and so the currency pound, but POUND comes from the enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: The foot-pound is an imperial measure of energy: lifting one pound through one foot.

clue.text: Harshly criticise the Spanish jury

parts.note: to pan is to slate or review savagely
el is Spanish for 'the'

explanation.surface: Someone attacks the verdict of a jury in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: PAN is followed by EL.
explanation.definitionFit: A jury is the group of people chosen to hear a case, and that list is called a panel.

clue.text: Was a tippler unpleasantly clammy? That's about right

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece is placed round another

parts.note: dank means unpleasantly damp and cold
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Was the drunkard sweaty? Someone says that is about right.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark splits the clue: the definition comes first, DANK and R the wordplay after.
explanation.definitionFit: A tippler is a habitual drinker, so being one means having downed alcohol regularly.

clue.text: Own goal by reserve — very bad-tempered people!

parts.note: OG is the standard football abbreviation for own goal
res is short for reserve

explanation.surface: A substitute concedes an own goal and the team turns on him in fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' simply means next to, so the two abbreviations sit side by side; the exclamation mark plays up the fury of the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a monster of folk tales, so figuratively a cruel or fearsome, irascible person.

clue.text: Ready once for massive creature

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ready (cash) in old slang; 'once' marks it as dated
second meaning: a huge horned African or Asian beast

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' here is the British slang noun for cash, as in 'the readies', and rhino was an old slang word for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhino served as Victorian slang for money, and is also the short name of the heavy horned mammal.

clue.text: Court without delay maintaining power

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold or keep, so one piece holds another inside

parts.note: soon means shortly, with little delay
P is the abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A law court acts promptly to keep its authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' looks like the legal noun but is the old verb for wooing.
explanation.definitionFit: To spoon is an old-fashioned word for to kiss and cuddle, which is what courting couples do.

clue.text: However complex tales will get learned

indicators.note: complex means intricate or tangled, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
wise means learned or knowledgeable

explanation.surface: However involved the stories, they will be learnt by heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Learned' reads as the verb learnt, but here it is the adjective, meaning scholarly.
explanation.definitionFit: Leastwise is an informal sentence adverb like 'at any rate', introducing a qualification as 'however' does.

clue.text: Feelings of allegiance to monarchy taking on new direction

definitions.note: plural phrase; the answer is a singular noun

indicators.note: taking on a new direction means swapping one compass or side letter for another

parts.note: royalty is the monarch and family, so the institution of monarchy
L for left replaces R for right

explanation.surface: Patriotic devotion to the Crown that changes course.
explanation.walkthrough: In ROYALTY the R (right) turns into L (left), the other direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Loyalty is faithfulness and devotion, the sense of owing support to a cause or ruler.

clue.text: Ambiguously worked around unknown significant group of letters

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece is placed outside another
ambiguously means open to more than one reading, so the letters may be read in another order

parts.note: taken as written
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A cryptic message was vaguely worked out around a mystery set of letters.
explanation.walkthrough: WORKED is rearranged and then wraps round Y, the algebraic unknown.
explanation.definitionFit: A keyword is an important word, one that unlocks a cipher or indexes a search.
